candidates.name: Jon Husted
candidates.background: Official Senate biography: elected to the Ohio House in 2000 and served as Speaker from 2005 to 2009; later served in the Ohio Senate, as Ohio Secretary of State for two terms, and as Lieutenant Governor. He began serving in the U.S. Senate in January 2025. In his biography, Husted says he was born into foster care and adopted.
promises: Says his work focuses on lowering costs for working families and supports the Working Families Tax Cut Act.
Supports streamlining federal permitting for energy and mineral infrastructure, which he says can lower costs.
Introduced the Upward Mobility Act, proposing a five-state pilot to test changes intended to reduce benefits cliffs.
Says he supports stronger border security and law-enforcement funding.
Introduced the Ratepayer Protection Act, proposing that state regulators consider requiring large new electricity users to cover the incremental grid costs they create.
His Senate biography describes him as a pro-family advocate and says he has worked to protect unborn children.
record: Voted YEA on final passage of H.R. 1 on July 1, 2025. The Senate recorded 50–50; the Vice President cast the tie-breaking vote.
Voted YEA on final passage of S. 2, the Secure America Act, on June 5, 2026.
Introduced S. 5028, the Ratepayer Protection Act. After the House passed companion H.R. 9340 by 417–3, a Senate cloture vote on the motion to proceed to H.R. 9340 failed 57–43 on September 30, 2026.
Voted NAY on cloture on the motion to proceed to S. 2882 on October 9, 2025 (47–50). The bill included a permanent extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits.
Voted YEA on cloture on S. 6, the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act, on January 22, 2025; the motion failed 52–47.
Voted NAY on a motion to discharge S.J.Res. 104, a resolution directing removal of U.S. forces from unauthorized hostilities with Iran; the motion failed 47–53 on March 4, 2026.
